hint: Return the text of one SSE event: "event: <type>", then "data: <line>" for each data line, each line ended by a newline, and one empty line at the end.

Return a Ring response map: status 200, Content-Type text/event-stream, Cache-Control no-cache, and a body that is one datastar-patch-elements event whose single data line is "elements " followed by the greeting HTML.

Return the event text in this order: "event: <type>", then "id: <id>" when id is given, then "retry: <ms>" when retry is given and is not 1000, then "data: <line>" for each data line, then one empty line. Every line ends with "\n".

Build the data lines, leaving out defaults: "selector …" if given, "mode …" unless outer, "useViewTransition true" if true, "viewTransitionSelector …" if given with a view transition, "namespace …" unless html, then "elements <line>" for each line of the HTML (none when html is nil). Send them with send-event.
Encode signals as JSON unless it is already a string. Send "onlyIfMissing true" first when that option is true, then "signals <line>" for each line of the JSON.
Make a <script> tag with each attribute as name="value", plus data-effect="el.remove()" when auto-remove is on. Send it as a patch-elements event that appends to the selector body.
Add the drink's base price, the size delta, and the milk delta (no milk adds nothing).
Take the JSON text from the "datastar" query parameter for GET and DELETE, and from the request body for other methods. Parse it with keyword keys. Return {} when there is nothing to read.
Make a draft from the signals. If it has an error, patch {quote: 0, error: <message>}. Otherwise patch {quote: price × qty, error: ""}. Return a one-shot SSE response.

Return hiccup for div#drink-options. It holds select#size (data-bind:size) with one option per size of the drink, and select#milk (data-bind:milk) with one option per milk, or [:p.muted "No milk"] when the drink takes no milk. Mark the chosen size and milk as selected. A sold-out milk is disabled and its label ends with " (sold out)".

Read drink, size and milk from the signals. Find the valid choice. Send two events: first patch #drink-options with the view, then patch only the signals that changed (size, milk). A missing milk is sent as "" so the bound select keeps a string.
Return nil when draft-error finds a problem (use the state's sold-out set). Otherwise add the line {:drink :size :milk :qty} to the end of the cart for sid and return the new state.

Return the next state for each command type: :add-to-cart (append line to sid's cart when line-error is nil), :remove-from-cart (drop the line at idx), :place-order (turn a non-empty cart into a :placed order for a non-blank customer, then empty the cart), :advance (move an order one step along next-status; an order that reaches :picked-up leaves :orders), :toggle-stock (add or remove milk from :sold-out).
Return a one-shot SSE response that patches exactly the regions this command type changed (see the docstring), rendered from the new state.
Return a handler that calls `handler` only when the request header datastar-request is "true", and answers 403 otherwise.

Return the hiccup for <main id="app"> for this viewer: a customer sees the draft form, their own cart and only their own orders; the board sees every order and the milk stock. (customer-view and board-view are already written.)

For every subscriber in the hub, render (view-for state viewer) to an HTML string. If it differs from the subscriber's :last, call its send-fn with a patch-elements event of that HTML and record it as :last. Return the ids that were sent to.
Make a fresh id for this stream. On open, subscribe send-fn with the viewer and send it the whole current view right away (a reconnect must get the view again too). On close, unsubscribe it.
The shell appends `BrewShell/1` to its User-Agent. Return true when the request's user-agent header contains it, false otherwise (including no header).
Return an execute-script event whose script calls window.BrewShell.post with msg as a JSON object literal. The JSON must be safe inside a <script> tag: a customer named "</script>" must not end it.
Return one {:sid … :message …} per order that is :ready in new but was not :ready in old, in order-id order. The message reads "Ada, your order #1 is ready."
